infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription: OnStandard uses the camera so you can photograph a meal and get instant nutrition feedback. Photos are analyzed for your log only.
infoPlist.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: OnStandard needs photo library access so you can pick an existing meal photo to log and analyze.
infoPlist.NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription: OnStandard can save a meal photo back to your library after you log it.
infoPlist.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: OnStandard confirms you arrived at practices, workouts and other commitments your coach scheduled. It checks your location only during a scheduled event window, records only whether you arrived and when, and never stores where you go.
infoPlist.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescrip: OnStandard can confirm you arrived at a scheduled commitment without you opening the app. It watches only the specific place your coach scheduled, only during that event window, and stores only whether you arrived and when — never a history of where you go.

privacyManifests._NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes_comment: Was an empty array, which declares 'this app collects nothing' — false, and a known rejection/removal trigger. Each entry below was traced to a real column or table, not assumed. Tracking is false throughout: there are no ad, attribution or third-party analytics SDKs, so there is no ATT prompt. NOT declared, deliberately: LOCATION. The geofence is evaluated on device and only arrived_at + a status cross the wire — commitment_responses has no lat/lng, and the coach's venue in commitment_locations is the coach's own data, not the athlete's whereabouts. Apple's question is about transmission, so 'no' is the accurate answer and should not be 'corrected' later. PURCHASES will need adding the day Stripe or IAP starts charging. FOUNDER: this is a legal attestation — confirm it against docs/go-live/APP-STORE-SETUP.md before you submit.

plugins._comment: backgroundColor is the app canvas (--bg #070B14), not the old brand blue. Launch used to flash a full screen of #1E50D6 and then cut to a near-black app, which is the single most visible 'unfinished' moment in the product because it happens every single open. Dark splash -> dark canvas -> the ring draws itself. NOTE: a splash change is native config, so it ships with the next BINARY, never over OTA.

plugins._comment: Wake-Up Roll Call lock screen. WITHOUT an appGroup this only declares NSSupportsLiveActivities (a plain Info.plist boolean, no capability, no code-signing impact) and asserts that modules/rollcall-live contributed its Android manifest. Pass { "appGroup": "group.com.onstandard.app" } ONLY after the App Group exists on the App ID and the provisioning profile carries it, or code-signing fails. See docs/go-live/ROLLCALL-LIVE-ACTIVITY.md.

READ ONLY, and deliberately minimal. The plugin turns background-delivery ON by default and writes an UPDATE usage string by default; we want neither. OnStandard never writes to Health and never reads in the background, so declaring either would be asking for a permission the app does not use, which is both dishonest and an App Review flag. background:false also keeps com.apple.developer.healthkit.background-delivery out of the entitlements, so the provisioning profile only has to carry com.apple.developer.healthkit.
plugins.NSHealthShareUsageDescription: OnStandard reads last night's sleep, heart rate variability and resting heart rate so your recovery check-in has real context next to what you reported. It is read-only, it never changes your score, and nothing is ever written back to Health.
